rowData and colData of subsets in ExperimentSubset objects

Source: R/ExperimentSubset.R, R/SubsetRangedSummarizedExperiment.R, R/SubsetSingleCellExperiment.R, and 3 more
ExperimentSubset-rowData-colData.Rd

Get or set the rowData or colData of a subset by naming it with subsetName. Without subsetName, these methods act on the main object, as for the class x extends.

A subset stores only its own columns. With parentRowData = TRUE or parentColData = TRUE, the main object's columns come first, for the subset's rows or columns, and a subset's own column hides the main object's column of the same name, with a message if their values differ. When setting a subset's data, columns that came from the main object, in data read with parentRowData = TRUE or parentColData = TRUE, are left out with a message, so only the subset's own are stored. To add one column, use colData(x, subsetName = "name")$column <- values.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'SubsetRangedSummarizedExperiment'
rowData(x, use.names = TRUE, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SubsetRangedSummarizedExperiment'
colData(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SubsetRangedSummarizedExperiment'
rowData(x, ...) <- value

# S4 method for class 'SubsetRangedSummarizedExperiment,DataFrame'
colData(x, ...) <- value

# S4 method for class 'SubsetRangedSummarizedExperiment,NULL'
colData(x, ...) <- value

# S4 method for class 'SubsetRangedSummarizedExperiment,data.frame'
colData(x, ...) <- value

# S4 method for class 'SubsetSingleCellExperiment'

Arguments

x

An ExperimentSubset object.

use.names

logical(1) Whether the rowData returned has row names. Default TRUE.

...
subsetName

character(1) Name of the subset whose data to get or set. Leave it out for the main object's.

parentRowData

logical(1) For rowData() of a subset, whether to include the main object's columns. Default FALSE.

parentColData

logical(1) For colData() of a subset, whether to include the main object's columns. Default FALSE.

Without subsetName, other arguments are passed on to the method of the class x extends.

value

A DataFrame with one row per row (rowData<-) or column (colData<-) of the subset or the main object, or NULL to remove all columns (a SpatialExperiment keeps its sample_id column). For a subset, a data.frame is also accepted and converted to a DataFrame; for the main object, colData<- with a data.frame is an error.

Value

rowData() and colData() return a DataFrame. The setters return x with the data set.

See also

subsetRowData, subsetColData, rowData, colData

Examples

# an object with 10 genes and 20 cells
set.seed(1)
counts <- matrix(rpois(200, lambda = 5), nrow = 10)
rownames(counts) <- paste0("gene", 1:10)
colnames(counts) <- paste0("cell", 1:20)
es <- ExperimentSubset(list(counts = counts))
# a sample label for every cell of the main object
es$sample <- rep(c("A", "B"), each = 10)
# a subset of the first 5 genes and the first 8 cells
es <- createSubset(es, subsetName = "first", rows = 1:5, cols = 1:8)
# a cluster label for each of the subset's 8 cells
colData(es, subsetName = "first")$cluster <- rep(1:2, times = 4)
# the subset's own columns
colData(es, subsetName = "first")
#> DataFrame with 8 rows and 1 column
#>         cluster
#>       <integer>
#> cell1         1
#> cell2         2
#> cell3         1
#> cell4         2
#> cell5         1
#> cell6         2
#> cell7         1
#> cell8         2
# with the main object's columns first
colData(es, subsetName = "first", parentColData = TRUE)
#> DataFrame with 8 rows and 2 columns
#>            sample   cluster
#>       <character> <integer>
#> cell1           A         1
#> cell2           A         2
#> cell3           A         1
#> cell4           A         2
#> cell5           A         1
#> cell6           A         2
#> cell7           A         1
#> cell8           A         2
# the subset's rowData, which has no columns yet
rowData(es, subsetName = "first")
#> DataFrame with 5 rows and 0 columns
